why: Intro to Git and GitHub plan (docs/ui-next/catalog/plans/intro-git.json), 'Undo a change and ignore files' (passes: .gitignore lists .DS_Store and is committed, ...). The learner wrote the file and skipped `git add`, trusting `git commit -am` to pick it up. -a only stages files git already tracks: the new .gitignore stays untracked and git answers 'nothing added to commit but untracked files present'. .gitignore holds the line, but it is not committed; 'Ignore .DS_Store' is only the typed message.

step.title: Ignore .DS_Store
step.instructions: Make a .gitignore with one line, .DS_Store (echo .DS_Store > .gitignore). Then stage it and commit it: git add .gitignore and git commit -m "Ignore .DS_Store".
